name: Wireless Zone Thermostat

steps.text: Choose a spot out of direct sun and away from HVAC vents and fans.
Insert 2 AA batteries; high-quality alkaline batteries are recommended.
Close the cover.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the display shows temperature and humidity, mode Off, a full battery and 12:00PM

steps.text: Snap the Wireless Zone Thermostat into the tabletop stand or mount it on a wall.

notes: It does not control the HVAC system itself; it talks over RF to a Thermostat 2441TH wired to the HVAC system. Up to two can be added to one Thermostat.

Optionally connect a 5.0V, 200mA AC/DC adapter (no more than 5.5V) to the two left screws of the terminal block, observing polarity; on external power it stays awake all the time and supports Day Mode.
It needs at least one dual-band Insteon device to reach powerline devices.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Wireless Zone Thermostat beeps.
Tap the Up or Down arrow to choose the group to link: 1 cooling (default), 2 heating, 3 dehumidification, 4 humidification.

notes: Then adjust the responder to the state you want and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps or its LED flashes. The Wireless Zone Thermostat double-beeps and its LED turns off.

To add it to a wired Thermostat 2441TH: press and hold its SET button until it beeps (SET LED blinks green), then press and hold the wired Thermostat's SET button until it double-beeps; the Wireless Zone Thermostat double-beeps too.
When linked to a wired Thermostat, its group commands to other responders don't work.

steps.text: Press the Program or Time/Sensor button to wake the Wireless Zone Thermostat from its battery-saving mode.
To keep it awake for programming, send Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20, extended) with cmd2 0x06 (stay awake); it stays awake for 4 minutes.
Press and hold the SET button until the Wireless Zone Thermostat beeps.
Tap the Up or Down arrow to choose the group to link: 1 cooling (default), 2 heating, 3 dehumidification, 4 humidification.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: While the device is still awake, have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.
When done, have the Hub send Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20, extended) with cmd2 0x07 to let the Wireless Zone Thermostat sleep again.

notes: Put the device in linking mode before the Hub starts ALL-Linking. This links the device to the Hub as a controller, with the Hub as the responder, so the Hub receives the device's reports; the Hub makes no link to the device.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's waking and linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Wireless Zone Thermostat beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again.
Tap the Up or Down arrow to choose the group to remove (cooling is the default).

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button; the Wireless Zone Thermostat double-beeps and its LED turns off.
The Wireless Zone Thermostat 2441ZTH Owner's Manual recommends software for managing scene memberships whenever possible.

steps.text: Press the Program or Time/Sensor button to wake the Wireless Zone Thermostat from its battery-saving mode.
To keep it awake for programming, send Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20, extended) with cmd2 0x06 (stay awake); it stays awake for 4 minutes.

notes: The Wireless Zone Thermostat 2441ZTH Owner's Manual says the Program and Time/Sensor buttons wake it to retrieve updates from the wired Thermostat. The Wireless Thermostat Developer Notes list the stay-awake command (4 minutes) and the same command with cmd2 0x07, which puts it to sleep in 3 seconds.
On an external 5V power supply it stays awake all the time.

verification.note: The button step comes from the Wireless Zone Thermostat 2441ZTH Owner's Manual and the command from the Wireless Thermostat Developer Notes; neither document combines them into one procedure.

steps.text: Open the Wireless Zone Thermostat and remove one battery.
Wait 10 seconds.
While pressing and holding the SET button, reinsert the battery; don't let go of the SET button.
steps.expect: All segments blink and a long beep sounds for about 10 seconds

steps.text: When the blinking and beeping stop, release the SET button.
steps.expect: Self tests for about 10 seconds, then the display returns to normal

notes: Clears all scene memberships, sets the time to 12:00PM, and returns schedules, temperatures and other settings to their defaults; the temperature and humidity offsets are kept.

Alternative: press and hold the SET button until it beeps (LED blinks green), again until it beeps (LED blinks red), double-tap the SET button, then press and hold it until the blinking and long beep stop, and release.
If it shows a two-digit error code afterward, remove the batteries, wait a few seconds and reinstall them.
Before resetting, remove it from every controller's scenes.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Press the Program or Time/Sensor button to wake the Wireless Zone Thermostat from its battery-saving mode.
To keep it awake for programming, send Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20, extended) with cmd2 0x06 (stay awake); it stays awake for 4 minutes.
Press and hold the SET button until the Wireless Zone Thermostat beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again.
Tap the Up or Down arrow to choose the group to remove (cooling is the default).
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes the chosen group's link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes the chosen group's link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: When done, have the Hub send Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20, extended) with cmd2 0x07 to let the Wireless Zone Thermostat sleep again.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's waking and unlinking steps and the standard Insteon command Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Subcategories 0x11 and 0x12 are the European and Australian and New Zealand versions, the 2732-432 and 2732-532.
The Wireless Zone Thermostat 2441ZTH Owner's Manual gives subcategory 0x0A to the 2441ZTH, 0x11 to the 2732-432 and 0x12 to the 2732-532.
sources: Wireless Zone Thermostat 2441ZTH Quick Start Guide
